title: Qwen3-Omni MRv2 existing optimizations and streaming measurement boundaries
summary: Separate existing Qwen3-Omni MRv2 mechanisms from hardware qualification; profile predictor and grouped codec work while preserving request-to-audio latency, PCM versus codec frame units, and complete speech quality.

hardware: CUDA GPUs supported by the selected runtime; two L20X GPUs remain unqualified by this source audit
conditions: Full Thinker -> Talker -> Code2Wav streaming responses, with effective connector and stage configuration recorded.
The base deployment places Thinker on GPU 0 and Talker plus Code2Wav on GPU 1; its header reports two H100 GPUs, not L20X validation.
The experimental H200 overlay places all stages on GPU 0. Its configuration and comments do not establish two-GPU performance.

recommendations: Attribute sampled-token embedding handoff, Talker first-frame delivery, the codec chunk ramp, length-grouped multirow CUDA graphs, fused Snake, incremental predictor KV, short-KV attention, fused sampling and bounded cuDNN search to the existing upstream implementation. Enabling them on another SKU is an adaptation, not a new algorithm.

Use the MRv2 profile as an explicit control. It enables first-frame delivery, the chunk ramp and grouped codec graphs; the H200 overlay additionally opts into predictor KV, short-KV, fused sampling and cuDNN search. Change one mechanism per measured comparison.

If profiling attributes the bottleneck to predictor re-prefill, compare incremental KV and then short-KV separately; retain a control without fused sampling and cuDNN search. These options can change rounding and require full audio quality checks.

If profiling shows codec batch fragmentation, measure actual batch/window decode costs before tuning the fixed 32-frame-equivalent call-cost model. Configured graph batch sizes are constrained by batch times window length not exceeding the largest capture size; inspect actual captured shapes and group counts.

For colocated Talker and Code2Wav, compare MPS on/off under identical placement and memory budgets. Source guidance warns that throughput can improve while first-packet latency worsens; source inspection alone establishes neither effect on the target.

Define TTFA as first valid playable audio and retain the native audio_ttfp value separately if needed. The audited chat benchmark timestamps an audio-modality event before checking nonempty content; an empty event can precede the first audio bytes.

For the audited chat benchmark, audio RTF uses request start to last audio event divided by decoded audio duration. The reported mean is the arithmetic mean of request RTFs; it includes pre-audio Thinker work and is not a decoder-only ratio.

Native audio_frames counts PCM sample frames, while audio throughput is generated audio seconds per wall second. Label PCM frames/s and codec frames/s distinctly; derive codec rate only with explicit frame counts or validated sample-rate and codec-hop metadata.
validation_plan: Freeze workload, model weights, revisions, precision, input modalities, stage placement, sampling, warmup and complete output policy before performance comparisons. Retain failed requests and effective concurrency.
Record TTFA p50/p95, per-request RTF and its mean, explicitly named throughput units, audio duration, completion/error counts and streaming gaps for matched low and high concurrency runs.
Use traces to attribute predictor, codec, queueing and interstage costs before selecting changes; retain whole-run admission and drain costs alongside any steady-state slice.

Compare complete audio/text agreement and speech quality using the project benchmark methodology; retain repetitions, output-length differences and sampled-audio artifacts. CPU/catalog checks do not qualify GPU behavior.
limitations: Imported source guidance only: no local GPU run, measured gain, quality result or target attainment is claimed.
The source first-frame path requires CUDA, a local single-rank Talker, prefix caching disabled and a one-frame initial codec chunk. Other configurations retain the regular codec path.
Turn-mode measurements do not qualify duplex latency or interruption behavior.
The fixed call-cost calibration, H200 configuration and two-H100 deployment comments are not two-L20X evidence.
The benchmark timestamp and PCM frame observations apply to the pinned chat streaming implementation; other endpoints may use different timing and duration paths.
Source provenance revisions identify inspected implementation, not a baseline/candidate campaign or raw performance evidence.
